title: SDK Hub Connector — developer roadmap & quickstart sprint notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, pragmatic plan for the SDK Hub Connector: a single integration layer that lets product teams wire their frontends/backends to Redwood SDKs with consistent telemetry, sample app wiring, and a 10–15 minute quickstart. Goal is to reduce onboarding time and fragmentation across client libraries while preserving Redwood API ergonomics (hosted/dedicated/private).

Audience:
- SDK authors and maintainers
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers
- Product engineers embedding Redwood (hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private)

High-level outcomes we want from the sprint:
- Publish a working quickstart template (TypeScript + Python) that gets a dev from empty to a streaming chat demo in <= 15 minutes.
- A lightweight telemetry contract for all SDKs (events, token counts, latency, model metadata).
- A minimal connector library that standardizes auth plumbing, error handling, retry/backoff and local-mode stubbing.
- Docs and checklist for customers to map to Dedicated/Private deployment variants.

Core scenarios to support (prioritized):
1) Local dev -> Redwood hosted API: zero-config sample that streams responses and shows token-level cost in console.
2) Local dev -> Dedicated: sample config that demonstrates pinning model-version and a fallback route.
3) Private deployment example: VPC-aware connection snippet + KMS hint.
4) Offline/CI mode: a hermetic stub runner for deterministic integration tests.

Quickstart outline (README-first flow):
- Step 0: Prereqs (node 18+, python3.10, Docker optional)
- Step 1: clone repo (link) and install (npm/pip)
- Step 2: set REDWOOD_API_KEY (example: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx) and run local proxy script (./scripts/proxy.sh --local)
- Step 3: run ts example (npm run demo:ts) -> opens a terminal UI showing streaming tokens, token cost, per-request latency
- Step 4: swap to Dedicated config (instructions + commented config block) -> show pinning example and explain fallback policy
- Step 5: run python example (python demo/chat_quickstart.py) to validate cross-language parity
- Step 6: smoke tests and how to stub in CI (docker-compose or stub runner command)

Developer ergonomics and API surface (proposal):
- connector.createClient({ mode: 'hosted' | 'dedicated' | 'private', model: '...' , timeoutMs?: number, telemetry?: TelemetryOptions })
- client.chat.stream(messages, opts) -> async iterator / EventEmitter for token-level events
- client.chat.generate(messages, opts) -> promise for non-streaming use
- built-in helpers: attachTelemetry(ctx), wrapRetry(fn)

Telemetry contract (minimal v0):
- event: sdk.request.start -> { request_id, timestamp, sdk_version, client_lang, model_hint }
- event: sdk.request.token_chunk -> { request_id, tokens_out, token_type: prompt|completion, latency_ms }
- event: sdk.request.end -> { request_id, status: ok|error, tokens_total, cost_usd_estimate, latency_ms }
- event: sdk.env -> { env: hosted|dedicated|private, region, model_version }
- privacy note: do NOT log user prompts or PII by default; only send prompt hashes for regression detection.

Implementation notes / constraints:
- Keep connector surface tiny; avoid duplicating complex batching logic that belongs in runtime. This is an integration shim only.
- Telemetry should be pluggable; default sinks: console (dev), redwood-console via SDK key (prod), file for CI.
- Local stub runner will expose an HTTP endpoint that simulates streaming and reproduces common error modes (rate limit, kv-cache-miss).

Acceptance criteria for the first deliverable (MVP):
- README + TypeScript quickstart that completes in <= 15 minutes on a laptop with provided test key.
- Cross-language parity smoke test: TS and Python examples return same token counts for the same prompt within 1% variance.
- Telemetry events emitted according to contract for 100% of sample requests.
- CI stub runner included and used by at least one unit test in repo.

Rollout & docs plan:
- Week 1: Merge MVP quickstart and connector package as "alpha". Announce to internal SDK channels + seed developer advocate workshops.
- Week 2: Collect feedback, instrument failures and edge cases, iterate on README copy and error messages.
- Week 3: Add Java sample (optional) and update console-runbook with telemetry examples.

Open questions / risks (brain-dump):
- How opinionated should the connector be about retry/backoff vs. leaving that to callers? Proposal: provide safe defaults but expose hooks.
- Do we push token-cost calculations from client or compute in the Console from token counts? For quickstart compute locally (approx).
- Private deployments: do we need a different auth flow (mTLS) or can we reuse REDWOOD_API_KEY with a different endpoint? Need SRE input. (ping @infra-team)
- Stubbing fidelity: how many failure modes to simulate? Keep it small: rate limit, short-circuit error, and slow response for timeout testing.

Short TODO list (next actions):
- [ ] Draft README quickstart (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Implement minimal connector.createClient (owner: Evan)
- [ ] Python example parity smoke test (owner: Sofia)
- [ ] Stub runner basic HTTP stream behavior (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Draft telemetry schema PR and wire to redwood-console (owner: Maya)

Notes to self / rough copy for README top-of-file:
"This repo contains an intentionally small SDK Hub Connector. It helps you start with Redwood in minutes and demonstrates safe practices for telemetry, retries, and private deployment configuration. Pick a language, follow the quickstart, and open an issue if anything is unclear."

References & links (working):
- internal: RED-987 (Epic)
- github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-hub (main repo)
- console telemetry proto: confluence: Telemetry v1 draft
- related runtimes: serving-runtime/playbooks (link to drive)

Meeting snippets & rapid notes from 2024-10-22 sync:
- Evan: keep connector stateless, rely on runtime for batching
- Sofia: make token-metering visible in quickstart output (terminal + small HTML page)
- Liam: stub runner should be packaged as a small Docker image so SRE and CI can pull it
- Maya: prioritize docs that explain security differences between hosted/dedicated/private

End of sprint-note snapshot.

Unresolved items to surface in next retro:
- ownership for long-term maintenance and who will own SDK version bumps across languages.
- a decision on whether sample quickstart will include OpenTelemetry headers or a custom telemetry format.
